integrity: The proof starts from the primary source's exact boundary-oscillation formula for the analytic companion, performs the endpoint logarithmic integral explicitly, transfers the derivative estimate using the source's quasiregular inequalities, and integrates along radial-plus-angular paths. Sharpness is derived analytically from the exact Fourier series of the source's endpoint counterexample. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem gives an order-sharp log-Lipschitz endpoint modulus on the unit circle, not the best universal multiplicative constant for all distortion parameters. The exact coefficient 2/pi is established only for the analytic absolute-angle model. No conformally transported statement for arbitrary domains is claimed.
title: Sharp log-Lipschitz endpoint for real and imaginary parts of harmonic quasiregular maps
